nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: English First Additional Language Grade 4 Term 1

nodes.title: Weeks 1-2: Visual Information Text / Poster Advertising an Event
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to a visual information text / poster advertising an event; identify specific details; interpret the information given; relate to personal experiences. Reading and Viewing: Read a visual information text including elements such as graphics / tables / diagrams / maps / pictures etc.; pre-reading — make predictions based on title and pictures / visual images; use reading strategies such as skimming; ask and answer questions; discuss main idea; use vocabulary from context; read for comprehension; identify design features such as colour and different font sizes. Writing and Presenting: Write an information text like a report; organise information logically; develop supporting details; use appropriate tools such as maps and tables; use appropriate language, spelling and punctuation; plan, write a first draft and revise. Language Structures and Conventions: Work with words — articles, adjectives, abstract nouns, verbs, alphabetical order, synonyms and antonyms. Sentences — simple sentences. Spelling and punctuation.

nodes.title: Weeks 3-4: Novelette Extract (FAT 1 Oral begins)
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to and respond to an extract from a novelette; pre-reading strategies; listen for main idea and specific details; describe events; discuss social, moral and cultural values. Reading and Viewing: Read an extract from a novelette; use pre-reading strategies including skimming and predicting; identify and clarify main events; discuss characters; use a writing frame to summarise. Literature — Novelette / Reader must be read daily for at least 30 minutes. Reading methodology: Drop all and read / Group guided reading / Shared reading / Independent reading. Assess for learning — preparation for reading aloud. Writing and Presenting: Write a character sketch of the main character; use a writing frame; pre-write — listen to the extract from the novelette; choose appropriate language and text structure; organise information logically; write in chronological order. FAT 1 Oral: Read Aloud (20 marks) — begins in Term 1, concludes in Term 2 when mark is recorded.

assessmentStandards: FAT 1 Oral: Read Aloud 20 marks (starts T1, concludes T2)

nodes.title: Weeks 5-6: Short Story (FAT 1 Oral continues)
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to a short story; introductory activities — make predictions; identify main and supporting ideas; retell main events in the correct order. Reading and Viewing: Read a short story; use pre-reading strategies such as predicting from title and pictures; use reading strategies; identify new vocabulary from context; discuss the central idea, plot, characters and background; express feelings and opinions. Literature — Novelette continues. Writing and Presenting: Write a story based on a personal experience; select appropriate content; use appropriate structure and format; include characters; write paragraphs. Language Structures and Conventions: Work with words — abstract nouns, adjectives, number words, vowel group 3, alphabetical order, syllables and sound groups. Sentences — singular sentence, singular sentence (subject, predicate, object). Spelling and punctuation.

nodes.title: Weeks 7-8: Recipe (FAT 2 Writing)
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to and discuss a recipe; identify characteristics of instructional text; give clear instructions; ask questions for clarity about instructions; follow instructions. Reading and Viewing: Read a recipe; use pre-reading strategies; use reading strategies; identify specific details; identify the sequence of instructions; use comprehension strategies. Writing and Presenting: Write instructions on how to make something (e.g. a cup of tea); make a list of components and specific details; use correct sequence; use commands (imperatives); use correct structure and format. FAT 2 Writing: Essay (20 marks) — Narrative or descriptive, 3 paragraphs; task completed during the term.

assessmentStandards: FAT 2 Writing: Essay 20 marks — narrative/descriptive, 3 paragraphs

nodes.title: Weeks 9-10: Poster / Notices (FAT 3 Response to Texts)
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Take part in a short conversation on a familiar topic; make bets; stay on topic; ask relevant questions; tell own news; tell a story heard or read. Reading and Viewing: Read a poster or notice; discuss pictures; identify specific information; interpret the information; discuss purpose of the text; discuss language use; identify design features. Writing and Presenting: Design a poster advertising an event; choose appropriate information; use the correct format; use design features such as colour and different letter sizes or types. FAT 3 Response to Texts (40 marks): Literary / Non-literary text (15 marks), Visual text (10 marks), Language Structures and Conventions (15 marks).

assessmentStandards: FAT 3 Response to Texts 40 marks — Literary/Non-literary 15, Visual 10, Language 15

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: English First Additional Language Grade 4 Term 2

nodes.title: Weeks 1-2: Poem / Song / Limerick
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to a poem / song / limerick; identify the main idea / message; relate to own experience; identify rhythm; comment on the effect on the listener; express feelings evoked. Reading and Viewing: Read a poem / song from a textbook; discuss the main idea; express feelings; identify rhythm and rhyme; divide words into syllables to understand rhythm; use reading strategies and vocabulary strategies. Writing and Presenting: Write a simple poem / song; use appropriate content; use appropriate structure and format; plan, draft and revise; use appropriate rhythm and rhyme. Language Structures and Conventions: Abstract nouns, compound nouns, simile, alliteration, rhyme. Spelling and punctuation — spelling and spelling patterns, apostrophes, question marks.

nodes.title: Weeks 3-4: Weather Report / Chart / Table / Map (FAT 1 Oral concludes)
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to a weather report; listen for specific details; discuss usefulness of the information; compare conditions in different places; use interactional strategies effectively in group situations. Reading and Viewing: Read a weather report; identify similarities and differences; identify the way the text is organised; read an information text with visual elements such as maps or graphic representations; use reading strategies. Writing and Presenting: Write an information text with visual components such as a book cover / timeline; organise information logically. FAT 1 Oral concluded — mark recorded in Term 2.

assessmentStandards: FAT 1 Oral concluded in Term 2 — mark recorded

nodes.title: Weeks 5-6: Dialogue
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to a dialogue; predict; listen to determine relevance with own experience; identify specific details; role-play a scenario related to the selected novel in Term 1. Reading and Viewing: Read a dialogue; use reading strategies; identify main and supporting ideas. Writing and Presenting: Write a dialogue (short scene); choose appropriate content; use the framework; use direct and indirect speech; use appropriate grammar, spelling and punctuation. Language Structures and Conventions: Derivation, compounding, idioms, metaphor, proverbs, confusable words.

nodes.title: Weeks 7-8: Instructional Text / Directions / Rules (FAT 4 Transactional Writing)
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: Listen to and carry out instructions, e.g. directions / rules / safety rules; give clear instructions; take notes and apply instructions; ask questions for clarity; listen and give directions. Reading and Viewing: Read an instructional text such as directions / rules; use pre-reading strategies; identify specific details; identify the sequence of instructions. Writing and Presenting: Write an instructional text such as directions / rules; choose appropriate content; use appropriate structure; organise information logically. FAT 4 Transactional Writing (10 marks): Written before the June controlled test.

nodes.title: Weeks 9-10: Assessment of Read Aloud / Consolidation
nodes.description: Assessment of Read Aloud from the novelette studied in Term 1 and 2. Consolidation of all Term 1 and Term 2 content. Formal Assessment Summary: FAT 1 Oral — Read Aloud (20 marks); FAT 2 Writing — Essay, narrative/descriptive, 3 paragraphs (20 marks); FAT 3 Response to Texts (40 marks); FAT 4 Transactional Writing (10 marks).

assessmentStandards: Assessment of Read Aloud from novelette
